Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old male lawyer with 3–6 months of low mood, fatigue, reduced appetite, and unintentional weight loss, plus intermittent nausea/headaches and episodic palpitations/shortness of breath in elevators; history of hypothyroidism currently off levothyroxine; plan for baseline labs and safety-netting advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Low appetite and low energy; feeling “down.”
  - Intermittent nausea (no vomiting) and headaches (noted at work).
  - Episodic shortness of breath with palpitations in elevators; no chest pain; no cough.
  - Wife has noted problems with “nightly activities” (details not specified).
- Timeline:
  - Reduced appetite/low energy began ~3–3.5 months ago (after changing to new law firm).
  - Unintentional weight loss began earlier, estimated ~6 months.
  - Weight loss amount: patient said “less than a stone”; clinician summarized as “about a stone” over ~6 months (conflict noted).
  - Stopped levothyroxine since changing doctor; exact timing relative to symptom onset unclear.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Palpitations/SOB occur notably in elevators; patient does not identify specific food triggers for nausea; denies acid reflux.
  - Previously reported ability to walk a mile without dyspnea; later stated he hasn’t been walking recently, so exertional tolerance uncertain (conflict noted).
- Associated symptoms/pertinent negatives:
  - Bowels: normal frequency/consistency; no diarrhea; no blood or mucus; painless.
  - No vomiting. No chest pain. No cough. No known reflux.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid).
  - Previously treated with levothyroxine; currently not taking since changing doctor.
  - Last blood test: “a long time ago” (not specified).
  - Associated medication: Levothyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented); currently not taking.

Social History:
- Occupation: Lawyer; changed to a new law firm ~3–3.5 months ago.
- Home: Reports things “OK” at home; wife has noted concerns about sexual activity.
- Activity: Not walking/exercising lately due to feeling unwell.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substances: Not discussed.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam: Not performed during this telehealth visit.

Investigations:
- None performed today.
- Planned: “General set of bloods” including screening for anemia, kidney function, liver function, and vitamin levels (specific vitamins not detailed). Additional tests not explicitly listed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Low mood, fatigue, reduced appetite, and unintentional weight loss (3–6 months).
  - Etiology unclear; medical causes to be evaluated.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange baseline labs: CBC (anemia screen), renal function, liver function, vitamin levels (per clinician plan).
    - Review results and proceed to in-person physical examination if labs are unremarkable.
    - Safety net: seek care if weight loss accelerates, new vomiting occurs, or bowel habit changes develop.
    - Follow-up: Patient will receive a text to book an appointment once results are available; advised to contact clinic sooner if feeling worse.
- Issue 2: Episodic palpitations and shortness of breath in elevators; no chest pain; no clear exertional dyspnea reported earlier but activity limited currently.
  - Plan:
    - Include in evaluation with baseline labs.
    - Safety net: go to the emergency department immediately if chest pain develops or if palpitations/SOB become severe or persistent.
- Issue 3: History of hypothyroidism; currently off levothyroxine; no recent labs.
  - Plan:
    - Evaluate with baseline labs as above; further thyroid assessment and medication review to follow after results (no medication changes made today).
- Issue 4: Intermittent nausea and headaches.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor symptoms; included in baseline lab evaluation.
    - Safety net: contact clinic if vomiting develops or if bowel habits change.

- General plan items:
  - Patient instructed to call support via the app to arrange blood tests; clinician will submit the lab request form.
  - Patient will receive text notification for follow-up appointment after results.
  - Advised to contact clinic if condition worsens; emergency department for acute chest pain or severe palpitations/SOB.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies.
  - Full medication list and reconciliation (including OTC/supplements).
  - Surgical history.
  - Family history.
  - Vitals and physical exam.
  - Mental health screening (e.g., PHQ-9), suicidality assessment.
  - Substance use, smoking, and alcohol history.
  - Exact weight/BMI and objective weight trend.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Weight loss amount: patient “less than a stone” vs clinician “about a stone.”
  - Exertional tolerance: initially “can walk a mile without SOB” vs later “hasn’t been walking lately,” making exertional dyspnea assessment uncertain.
  - Symptom timing relative to stopping levothyroxine is uncertain.
- Transcript quality:
  - Several brief inaudible/unclear segments and interruptions; some statements were partially cut off. Overall history obtained but with minor ambiguities.
